simd_load_wide_r2.formula:
src = C*ISB ; [x]+ = max(0,x)
A. src >= 32 B  (wide contiguous-block path)   : T = 67.41 + 2.980*R + 2.176*R*[eb-4]+      (n=157, MAPE 12.51%)
B. src <  32 B and C >= 4 (short-row fallback) : T = 145.7 + 5.384*n + 0.4251*span         (n=33,  MAPE 11.06%)
C. src <  32 B and C == 1 (degenerate column)  : T = 97.97 + 3.273*n                        (n=32,  MAPE 18.05%)

terms.name: A.const
terms.meaning: MTE2 fixed start-up / first-byte latency - reproduces the 65.34 ns constant of simd_load_wide_r1

terms.name: A.R
terms.meaning: per-row descriptor issue cost on the wide path (ns/row)

terms.name: A.R*[eb-4]+
terms.meaning: extra per-row cost for elements wider than 4 B (int64: +8.7 ns/row); the row is handled as more than one 4-B transaction

terms.name: B.const
terms.meaning: fixed cost of the fallback path for a real 2-D tile

terms.name: B.n
terms.meaning: per-ELEMENT command cost when a row is too short for a block transfer (ns/element)

terms.name: B.span
terms.meaning: address-spread cost of the fallback walk (ns per byte of tile span)

terms.name: C.const
terms.meaning: fixed cost of a degenerate (R,1) column load

terms.name: C.n
terms.meaning: per-element cost of the degenerate 1-D column load (ns/element)

derived: R,C = tile rows/cols (R>=2; R==1 shapes are 1-D and dropped)
ISB = inner stride bytes (2*eb for C>=2, eb for C==1)
rb = (C-1)*ISB + eb     = contiguous byte footprint of one row
src = C*ISB             = source bytes spanned by one row's strided pattern (= rb + eb when IS=2)
span = (R-1)*pitch + rb = total tile address footprint (bytes)
GATE: src >= 32 B  <=>  a row's strided source covers at least one full 32-B memory sector

worst10: R=4 C=1 eb=4 src=4 rb=4 pitch=64 n=4 T=358.4 pred=111.1 err=-69%
R=16 C=1 eb=1 src=1 rb=1 pitch=16 n=16 T=296.0 pred=150.3 err=-49%
R=16 C=1 eb=4 src=4 rb=4 pitch=8 n=16 T=265.5 pred=150.3 err=-43%

simd_load_wide_r2.notes: GATE (the key new finding). For every C>=2 row IS=2, hence src = C*ISB = rb + eb. The 222 points split EXACTLY at src = 32 B: 157 points with src>=32 have T in [70.7, 547.9]; 65 points with src<32 have T in [90.9, 2528.0]. src<32 means one row's strided source does not even cover a single 32-B memory sector, so the compiler cannot use the contiguous block-copy + extract_slice lowering (the one confirmed for the wide branch) and the load degenerates to a per-element strided-command path that costs 10-30x more per element. On this grid src>=32 is simultaneously equivalent to C*eb>=16 (>=16 B of payload per row) and to rb >= 32-eb; the data cannot separate these three readings, and no measured shape falls between rb=15 and rb=28. This is why forms such as T = a + b*R*max(32,row_bytes) stall at 26-28%: they model only branch A, and branch A is not byte-driven at all. BRANCH A physics: after the block path is available the cost is 67 ns of start-up plus ~3 ns per row descriptor, plus a large per-row penalty for 8-B elements. Bytes moved (R*rb) and element count n are nearly irrelevant inside A - (R=16,C=8,eb=4,rb=60)=110.9 ns and (R=16,C=16,eb=4,rb=124)=107.1 ns; at fixed R=16,eb=8 the whole C range 4..32 moves T only from 303 to 341 ns, while at fixed n=64 the R range 4..16 moves T from 120 to 303 ns - so branch A is descriptor/row driven, not byte driven. BRANCH B physics: per-element command cost (5.38 ns/elem) plus an address-spread term (0.43 ns per byte of span); same shape as simd_load_gather_r1 but with a far larger per-element constant. BRANCH C: C==1 tiles have no inner dimension, so ISB is meaningless - these 32 points are really 1-D strided loads that the slot rule put here because ISB=eb<=2*eb. They are internally inconsistent (for int8/int64 a larger pitch is FASTER, for float16/float32 SLOWER), so only a 2-term form is defensible; the 1-D formula simd_load_wide_r1 (65.34+0.008652*span) gives 50.5% on them and does NOT transfer. VERDICT: the 8-coefficient physical model (13.10%) BEATS the user's greedy (17.10%, 17 items) and comes within 0.7 pt of a 17-term greedy over a 76-feature library (12.39%); with 15 coefficients it matches it (12.27%). A 2-branch variant that folds C==1 into branch B (T = 77.22 + 8.979*n - 0.06528*span) gives 15.68%. REMAINING RESIDUAL (median 11.2%, p90 26.8%, max 69%) has no structure we could tie to a physical quantity: the worst points are R=4 int64 rows (block path, over-predicted because the int64 per-row penalty is not yet active at R=4) and C==1 columns. The slot also carries irreducible measurement noise (target_spread up to 0.97).
